show: That's Messed Up: An SVU Podcast

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen (Abruf laeuft ueber den Werbedienst podtrac.com) - zu wenig fuer ein Urteil, aber nicht nichts; Ausschnitte dieser Sendung waren in zwei Messungen mit Stunden Abstand stumm - die Datei wird je Abruf neu zusammengesetzt

einzeiler: A deep dive into Law and Order: SVU season six, episode nine, "Weak".
kurzfassung: The hosts recap Law and Order: SVU season six, episode nine, titled "Weak". They discuss the episode's plot, featuring a serial perpetrator targeting vulnerable women, and guest star Amanda Plummer's Emmy-winning performance. They also explore the real-life criminal cases that inspired the episode.
stichpunkte: Recap of Law and Order: SVU season six, episode nine, "Weak"
Discussion of guest star Amanda Plummer's Emmy-winning role as a witness with schizophrenia
Analysis of the perpetrator's modus operandi targeting women with vulnerabilities
Exploration of the real-life Center City rapist case involving Troy Graves
Comparison to the crimes of Richard Speck and nurse nursing student murders
Examination of police and prosecutorial handling of sexual assault cases
Mention of podcast guests and actors who appeared across multiple SVU episodes

kapitel.titel: True Crime Deep Dive and Real-Life Cases

clips.hook: Swimming with leopard sharks in La Jolla
clips.text: The hosts reflect on the positive energy of their recent live tour and express appreciation for the themed presents received from fans.
The hosts encourage listeners to support educators by fulfilling supply requests posted on a community wish list.

clips.hook: Consensual sex and trauma in psychiatric patients
clips.text: The discussion explores the complex intersection of PTSD and schizophrenia, focusing on a character's struggle to distinguish traumatic memories from reality.

clips.hook: The medical twist behind the DNA mismatch
clips.text: The hosts note their success in interviewing nearly every cast member from the current episode and express regret over missing a chance to feature Hetty.

clips.hook: Richard Speck's chilling prison interview quote
clips.text: A psychiatric evaluation reveals a character's obsessive-compulsive personality disorder and his tendency to categorize women into rigid, binary archetypes.
